required: Any work that gets someone in (a lockout, a rekey, new locks): the entry statement, a form signed on the secure page while the time is saved (10 minutes). It's kept with that job only.

pf.visit.check-in: The check-in code at the door, or at the counter. Then, before any lock is opened or changed, the locksmith checks a photo ID against proof of the right to enter, in the same name.
pf.visit.door rule: No proof, or someone at the door objects: no lock is touched, and the locksmith leaves. That's the customer's side: the $89 trip fee Alex agreed to only if Sam confirms; no answer, no fee. Alex can book again with proof.
pf.visit.work changes: Picking first. Drilling or a new lock is quoted at the door and done only after the customer's yes, on their phone or on the locksmith's phone when theirs is locked inside. Other work is quoted for another day.
pf.visit.record: Where the state's rules require it, an opening record on a secure page: the name, the address or car, the kind of ID and proof shown, the time and how it was opened. Kept apart from job notes; only the owner opens it.
pf.visit.proves it's done: The code, then DONE; the opening record is finished before DONE where required.
pf.visit.at the counter: A car key needs a photo ID and the registration in the same name; a high-security key needs its key card.

pf.money.before: At the customer's place: the a card saved for the $89 trip fee at booking (a lockout is within the hour, so it's held at once). At the counter: nothing, or a card saved for the $20 fee.
pf.money.after: Rosie texts the bill when the locksmith texts DONE with the lines; the card on the locksmith's phone, or cash, also work.
pf.money.after-hours price: Lockouts at night and on Sundays have an after-hours price, shown in full before anyone is sent.
pf.money.cancel: Lockouts: free until the locksmith heads out; after that, the $89 trip fee, only if Sam confirms. Set-window jobs: free until the free-cancel time.
pf.money.no proof at the door: The customer's side: the $89 trip fee Alex agreed to may come from the hold, only if Sam confirms. No answer in 24 hours: released, no fee.
pf.money.emergency prices: Where the state's rules limit prices in a declared emergency, those limits apply.
pf.money.written estimate: above the amount in the state's form
pf.money.tax: on parts, where the state's form says so

pf.staff.licenses: Each locksmith's own license, where the state's rules require one. An apprentice works only with a licensed locksmith on the job.
skills: Alarm work: only people with the alarm license
pf.staff.on call: Sam sets who takes sent-now jobs in open hours and who's on call at night, on weekends and holidays, each with a backup. The one on call gets urgent texts at any hour and takes a lockout by reply within 5 minutes; then the backup.
pf.staff.stand-ins: A stand-in must hold the same license and skill. A new person at the door is offered first, never assumed.
pf.staff.who OKs what: Sam OKs prices over $500 made for one customer. Pat may OK them too; Sam's answer wins.

pf.rules.records: Opening records kept for the state's period, where its rules require them; a delete request can't remove them early.
pf.rules.license number: Shown on the listing, quotes, the confirmation and receipts, where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.written estimate: For work above an amount, where the state's rules set one.
pf.rules.right to cancel: Work sold at the home comes with a written right to cancel, for the period the state's rules set.
pf.rules.lockout limit: One lockout a day per phone and per address, across every business on Rosie.
pf.rules.status: Draft: finalized once the state forms are filled in.

matter most.a renter wants a rekey or new locks: The landlord's OK on the page first.

notes:
Flow B's main story stays on the master's set-window timeline: a whole-home rekey at 27 Oak St, Thu Oct 22, 8 to 10am. The master's dates run through every step and its money variants, so a same-night lockout can't replace them by renaming.
The urgent lockout uses the master's sent-now steps (v1.1): the offer with the after-hours price in full first (B4-19, words), the locksmith on call then the backup (S2-27, B6-16 to B6-18), no reminder and free cancel until OMW (B7-48 to B7-50). Only locksmith lines are added there (B6-16, B7-48).
Identity comes first on every visit at the customer's place, not only lockouts (a rekey needs the right to enter too): the entry questions before any times (B4-x01), the entry statement as the master's form on the secure page (B4-38's form branch, B4-86, due while the time is saved), and the ID-and-proof check at the door before any lock is touched (B8-45, the master's 'Is anything required missing?'). No match or an objection is 'Missing: can't go ahead' (B8-54).
The master's money numbers are kept: the $89 service call is the $89 trip fee, the $179 drain clearing a whole-home rekey, the $150 flush a smart lock install, the $640 water heater high-security locks priced from photos. The lockout is $159 by day and $199 after hours ($89 trip + $110 opening): the example business's own prices.
Flow A is the key shop counter (Lee's Key Shop, the master's second company): rekeys of locks brought in, key copies, car keys, high-security keys, a master key set, antique lock repair from photos, and lock repair priced at the bench. The master's color services became antique lock work; its patch test became a key card check for restricted keys.
Main money paths: A list|none|counter (a key counter rarely saves a card for a $35 rekey); B list|hold|bill (Rosie's default at the customer's place, and right for a lockout: the trip fee held).
One rename list serves both flows, since the shared sections (sign-up, team, running the business) hold both stories. Whole master sentences are swapped first where word-by-word swaps would garble a story; no keep words were needed.
Names: Jordan is Tomás (the old flowchart's on-call locksmith), Casey is Andre (the master calls him he), Riley and Avery are Marco and Lena. The second kind of work under Lee Lock & Key is alarm work, with its own state form and an alarm tech, like the master's electrical.
Turned off in flow A: 'Yes, with a parent' of A4-70 (an adult books lock work; a child booking gets the master's 'adults only', and a teen asks a parent) and 'A reaction last time' of A4-43 (lock work has no health step).
Master v1.1 took the locksmith's general ideas: the on-call dispatch (G1), the visit that can't go ahead (G11, B8-54), the visit record (G12, B8-55 and B8-56: the opening record's fields are a more line) and the phone or address limit (G23, S12-28: the one-lockout-a-day cap is a more line and in the plug-in). The own steps that drew them (B4-x06, B6-x01 to B6-x04, B8-x01 to B8-x04) are gone.
No proof at the door, or someone there who objects, is the customer's side in master v1.2 (D35, B8-60): Alex said at booking there was proof and that nobody objects. So the $89 trip fee Alex agreed to may be charged, only if Sam confirms; no answer, no fee. That's the old flowchart's trip-fee question again (lk20b). The trip fee also applies to a cancel after OMW, only if Sam confirms.
Money: no visit+deposit path. Lee Lock & Key holds the $89 trip fee for work priced at the visit; it never takes it as a deposit.
The old flowchart's one-state facts (an NC license, a 3-year record, a 5-business-day cancel right) are switches now, filled from the state's form. Its Workiz parts are outdated: Rosie is the software.
The old $75 trip-fee link (lk18f, lk20c) is now a fee taken from the hold or the saved card, Sam confirming first, the way the master draws every fee.
Not sure: the urgent pattern may deserve the lockout as flow B's main path. That needs an urgent variant of the master's flow B timeline (sent now, no day-before steps), so it's listed as a gap rather than rewritten here.
Master v1.2 (D24): at every plug-in split the locksmith keeps its own branch and turns the others off. Both flows: the $2, no added agreement, people not spaces, no classes, lockouts sent now, every booking by name. The license splits (S1-60, S1-63, S2-28) keep both branches: only some states license locksmiths. Flow A (the key shop): walk-ins wait in a line; a locksmith's time, no drop-offs; adults only; no form, no damage hold, no crew, no date that can't move, no minimum; late means a shorter visit or a later start; it's rated.
Flow B (the home, car or business): sent now (lockouts) or soonest first (rekeys); arrival windows; own or rent asked, or skipped for a car; a contract over the plug-in's amount; the entry statement is the only first step (B4-38's other branches are off, and so are B7-05's late-form and first-step branches); no damage hold; one locksmith by name, never a crew; no group minimum; nothing missing can go on at the door; no outside check and no permit inspection.
Master v1.2 final (round 4): B4-83's new '4 A seat in a session' and '5 No person named' are off (every lock job names a locksmith). The new section 8 plug-in splits: an adult must be there when a child answers (B8-67); nobody home is never allowed (B8-69, B8-70: the plug-in's 'nobody home: never'); no service is delivered and set up (B8-71); a lock cylinder may go to the bench, so both branches of B8-72 stay on. A8-32's child branch is off, since the key shop books adults only (A4-70).
Plug-in splits kept whole (splitsKept, check-prof's D24 check), since the locksmith uses every branch: the license splits S1-60, S1-63, S2-28 in both flows (only some states license locksmiths); in A, A7-61 (antique locks have no stand-in) and A8-02 (locks, an ID and registration, or a key card to bring); in B, B4-81, B7-55, B8-58 (lockouts sent now, rekeys at a set time), B4-78 (own or rent for a home, skipped for a car), B4-57 (a written estimate over the state's amount) and B8-72 (a cylinder to the bench).
